summary: joule-btp-extension setup.py exfiltrates host files and environment at pip install
details: setup.py executes at pip install time and performs installer-side data collection and exfiltration. It reads /private/etc/passwd, /private/etc/hosts, and /private/etc/sudoers, dumps selected environment variables (HOME, USER, PATH, VIRTUAL_ENV, PIP_CACHE_DIR, npm_config_prefix, GIT_EDITOR), and recursively walks the current working directory and $HOME via glob, reading file contents (up to 4KB each). The collected JSON blob is POSTed to a hardcoded endpoint at http://127.0.0.1:4445/collect via urllib.request.urlopen, with all exceptions silently swallowed. setup.py additionally invokes os.system("cat /private/etc/passwd"), demonstrating shell execution from the install hook, and if VIRTUAL_ENV is set writes a marker file to $VIRTUAL_ENV/bin/.joule-btp-extension-was-here, showing capability to drop arbitrary content into the active virtualenv's bin directory. The module docstring self-identifies as a proof-of-concept sandbox-escape supply-chain payload, and a comment next to the hardcoded URL reads 'replace before deploying'.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
